observation: The earlier Caveman/Ponytail/Attention-Control recheck treated a small upstream delta too much like evidence that agent-loop already contained the relevant essence. A mechanism-level audit for PR #33 showed that source review and adaptation coverage are different claims. The deeper comparison surfaced useful mechanisms that were not represented strongly enough in the local contract: deterministic terminal states for narrow roles, bounded workflow-state restoration across session/subagent context loss, uncertainty preserved as explicit state, repeated-failure reset, and an explicit DEFER boundary for Ponytail-style cross-session simplification debt until agent-session owns a typed query. The first PR #33 CI run also demonstrated the same accuracy rule locally: runtime tests passed, but PHPStan rejected an overclaimed non-empty-string return type; the implementation was narrowed explicitly rather than weakening the contract or ignoring the discrepancy.

evidence.summary: Caveman at 14d4f2e21a16b573373ca24698cd6bd3db75bf52 was reviewed at the mechanism level across its core/review/compress/stats/commit skills, Cavecrew routing and investigator/builder/reviewer roles, activation hooks, and agent metadata. Ponytail at 2ed6c52c9d7e5e56942508591085fd45dea277d3 was reviewed across its core/review/audit/debt/gain skills, instruction builder, session/subagent hooks, mode tracking, and portability docs. Attention Control at 3c8a2a8a38f163aa85ad325812b5ce3ba330ad27 was reviewed for action/result-first output, state restoration, exact technical strings, uncertainty, and repeated-failure behavior. The resulting UPSTREAM_CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md records ALREADY/ADAPT/DEFER/REJECT per mechanism instead of inferring completeness from commit movement.

The first PR #33 iteration ran 341 PHPUnit tests successfully, then PHPStan rejected AgentDisciplineHook::readResumeManifest() because the declared non-empty-string task_id was not proven by the implementation. The fix added an explicit non-empty guard and kept the precise return contract; the manifest read was also made bounded directly instead of relying on a separate filesize precheck.
After the targeted fix, all three composer-ci matrix jobs passed. The self-shape job ran 341 PHPUnit tests with 1504 assertions and PHPStan reported no errors.

hypothesis: An external coding-agent project can be useful even when its newest commit adds little, because the local integration may still have failed to adapt an older mechanism. Therefore upstream maintenance must compare capabilities, not only commit deltas. Each mechanism needs an explicit local decision and owner/enforcement before agent-loop can claim it is represented; unresolved useful mechanisms must remain DEFER rather than being silently counted as adapted.
validated_conclusion: Future Caveman, Ponytail, Attention Control, or similar rechecks must update a mechanism-level capability inventory before making completeness claims. Classify each mechanism as ALREADY, ADAPT, DEFER, or REJECT; name the concrete agent-loop owner or reason; attach an observable test/dogfood/constraint where applicable; and revisit deferred/rejected rows when architecture or upstream behavior changes. A small upstream diff alone is not evidence that nothing relevant remains to adapt.
